clause.title: Two different schemas in the same block (action_schema, application_context_schema)
General
clause.p: The subject of the action_schema is the description of actions, the reasons for these actions, and the status of these actions.

example.p: Reasons for action include evolving user requirements, manufacturing problems and difficulties that arise when a product is in use.

sourcecode.body:
SCHEMA action_schema '{iso standard 10303 part(41) version(8) object(1) action_schema(1)}';
REFERENCE FROM basic_attribute_schema (description_attribute, description_attribute_select, get_description_value, get_id_value, get_name_value, get_role, id_attribute, id_attribute_select, name_attribute, name_attribute_select, object_role, role_select, role_association); REFERENCE FROM support_resource_schema (bag_to_set, identifier, label, text);

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: Action information can be attached to any aspect of product data.

clause.title: supported_item
clause.p:
The supported_item allows for the designation of an action_directive, an action, or an action_method.
This specifies the use of an action_resource.

clause.title: action
clause.p: An action is the identification of the occurrence of an activity and a description of its result.
An action identifies an activity that has taken place, is taking place, or is expected to take place in the future.

An action has a definition that is specified by an action_method.
In particular application domains, terms such as task, process, activity, operation, and event may be synonyms for action.

example.p: Change, distilling, design, a process to drill a hole, and a task such as training someone are examples of actions.

dd.p: the label by which the action is known.
the text that characterizes the action. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
the action_method that specifies the procedure selected to carry out the action and a description of the results of that action.
the identifier that distinguishes the action.

note.p: This attribute is an enhancement to the definition of action using a method that is upwardly compatible with ISO 10303-41:1994.

The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.

dd.p: Each action shall be the identified_item in at most one id_attribute.

clause.title: action_directive
clause.p: An action_directive is an authoritative instrument that provides directions to achieve the specified results.

example.p: ISO Directives Part 3 provides guidance for the development of standards documents within ISO.

dd.p: the label by which the action_directive is known.
the text that characterizes the action_directive. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

an informal description of the results of the analysis that was carried out on the elements of the requests set. The request sets are the versioned_action_requests referenced in the requests attribute.

note.p: The reason that different requests are satisfied by the action_directive could be recorded in this attribute.

dd.p: an informal description of any other pertinent information.
a set of versioned_action_request entity data types that defines the expected results.

clause.title: action_method
clause.p:
An action_method is the definition of an activity. This definition includes the activity’s objectives and effects.
This definition may be the basis for actions or the solution for action requests.

example.p: For the action whose name attribute is ‘serve dinner’, the name attribute of related instance of action_method could be ‘cook by recipe’ or ‘purchase takeout food’.

dd.p: the label by which the action_method is known.
the text that characterizes the action_method. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
an informal description of the effects of the action_method.
an informal description of the objectives of the action_method.

clause.title: action_method_relationship
clause.p:
An action_method_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type action_method and provides an identification and description of this relationship.
The role of action_method_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.
This entity, together with the action_method entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3.
This entity may be used to define a procedural relationship among constituent activities.

dd.p: the label by which the action_method_relationship is known.
the text that characterizes the action_method_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
one of the instances of action_method that is a part of the relationship.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the other instance of action_method that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other this attribute shall be the dependent one.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: action_relationship
clause.p:
An action_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type action and provides an identification and description of this relationship.
The role of action_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the label by which the action_relationship is known.
the text that characterizes the action_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
one of the instances of action that is a part of the relationship.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the other instance of action that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other this attribute shall be the dependent one.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: action_request_solution
clause.p: An action_request_solution is an association between a versioned_action_request and an action_method that is a potential solution for the request.

dd.p: the action_method that is a potential solution.
the versioned_action_request for which a solution is specified.
the text that characterizes the action_request_solution.

note.p: This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to action_request_solution as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994.

dd.p: the label by which the action_request_solution is known.

note.p: This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to action_request_solution as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994.

dd.p: Each action_request_solution shall be the described_item in at most one description_attribute.
Each action_request_solution shall be the named_item in at most one name_attribute.

clause.title: action_request_status
clause.p: An action_request_status is the association of a status with a versioned_action_request.

dd.p: the label that provides a user interpretable designation for the level of completion of the action.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the versioned_action_request to which the status applies.

clause.title: action_resource
clause.p: An action_resource is a thing that is identified as being needed to carry out an action.

dd.p: the label by which the action_resource is known.
the text that characterizes the action_resource. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
a set of supported_items for which the action_resource is used.
the action_resource_type that specifies the sort of action_resource that is being used.

clause.title: action_resource_relationship
clause.p:
An action_resource_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type action_resource and provides an identification and description of this relationship.
The role of action_resource_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.
This entity, together with the action_resource entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3.

dd.p: the label by which the action_resource_relationship is known.
the text that characterizes the action_resource_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
one of the instances of action_resource that is a part of the relationship.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the other instance of action_resource that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other this attribute shall be the dependent one.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: action_resource_type
clause.p: An action_resource_type is the identification of the kind of action_resource needed to carry out an action.

example.p: This entity may be used to specify the kind of tool needed to perform a process operation.

dd.p: the label by which the action_resource_type is known.

clause.title: action_status
clause.p:
An action_status is the association of a status with an executed_action.
Information about the date and time may be associated with the action_status through the use of date_assignment, date_and_time_assignment, or time_assignment.

dd.p: the label that provides a user interpretable designation for the level of completion of the action.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

example.p: Terms such as ‘pending’, ‘completed’, or ‘scheduled’ are examples of status.

dd.p: the executed_action to which the status applies.

clause.title: directed_action
clause.p: A directed_action is a type of executed_action that is governed by an action_directive.

example.p: A directed_action could be the inspection of a building as directed by city officials according to the city building codes for earthquake safety. The action is the inspection of the building. The directive is issued by city officials guided by the city building codes. In an application protocol, the building authority may be associated with an organization_assignment. The building codes may be associated with a document_reference.

dd.p: the action_directive that governs the directed_action.

clause.title: directed_action_assignment
clause.p: A directed_action_assignment is an association of a directed_action with product data.

dd.p: the instance of the directed_action entity data that is to be associated with product data.
the object_role that specifies the purpose of the association of the directed_action_assignment with product data.
Each directed_action_assignment shall be item_with_role in at most one role_association.

clause.title: executed_action
clause.p:
An executed_action is a type of action that is completed, partially completed, or just identified. It may but need not have status information associated with it.
The role of executed_action can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.
Status information is associated to executed_action through action_status.

example.p: An executed_action could be to ‘paint the office’ with a status of ‘scheduled’. The action is ‘paint the office’. The status further qualifies the action as ‘planned’, ‘scheduled’, or ‘completed’.

clause.title: versioned_action_request
clause.p:
A versioned_action_request is a specification of a desired result.
The desired result being identified and described may be obtained through one of more action_methods.

dd.p: the identifier that distinguishes the versioned_action_request.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the identification of the version of the versioned_action_request. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
an informal description of the reason for the versioned_action_request.
the text that characterizes the versioned_action_request. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

clause.title: versioned_action_request_relationship
clause.p:
A versioned_action_request_relationship is a relationship between two versioned_action_request objects.
Two versioned_action_request objects may be related if they address similar problems.
A versioned_action_request may be a version of a work request. It might be related to a different version of the work request using a versioned_action_request_relationship.

dd.p: the identifier that distinguishes the versioned_action_request_relationship.
the label by which the versioned_action_request_relationship is known.
the text that characterizes the versioned_action_request_relationship. The value of this attribute need not be specified.
one of the instances of versioned_action_request that is a part of the relationship.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the other instance of versioned_action_request that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other, this attribute shall be the dependent one.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: action_directive_relationship
clause.p: An action_directive_relationship is a relationship between two action_directive objects.

dd.p: shall be unique within a population of action_directive_relationship.
the text or the set of texts that provide further information about the action_directive_relationship. The value of this attribute need not be specified.
one object of action_directive that is part of the relationship.
the other object of action_directive that is part of the relationship.
the meaning of the relationship.
A action_directive_relationship shall not participate in its own definition.

clause.title: acyclic_action_method_relationship
clause.p: The acyclic_action_method_relationship function determines whether the graph of instances of the entity data type action_method that contains relation as one of its links contains a cycle. This function may be used to evaluate either an action_method_relationship or any of its subtypes.

The function returns TRUE if no cycle has been detected. Otherwise it returns FALSE.
The algorithm of the function is explained in annex E.2.
This function is not used in this schema. It is defined here because other ISO 10303 integrated resources and application protocols that use the action_method_relationship entity include rules that use this function.

clause.p: (input) the candidate action_method_relationship to be checked.

sourcecode.body: relation : action_method_relationship

clause.title: relatives
clause.p: (input) the set of instances of the entity data type action_method that the function is searching for in the relating_method parameter of the relation argument.

sourcecode.body: relatives : SET [1:?] OF action_method

clause.title: specific_relation
clause.p: (input) the fully qualified name of a subtype of the action_method_relationship entity.

sourcecode.body: specific_relation : STRING
x : SET OF action_method_relationship;

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the application_context_schema is the applicable usages of product data. This schema provides a mechanism for application protocols to define a frame of reference or context that applies to particular sets of product data.
This schema also provides a means to identify application protocols.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: The meaningful exchange of product data requires the identification of the application context in which that product data is defined. An application context may have several context elements. Each context element may be referenced by a different set of product data.

clause.title: exchange_identification_context_select
clause.p: The exchange_identification_context_select type allows for the designation of the data types identification_assignment and organization .

clause.title: application_context
clause.p: An application_context, as defined in ISO 10303-1, is a context in which product data is defined and has meaning. An application_context represents various types of information that relate to product data and may affect the meaning and usage of that data.

dd.p: the label by which the application_context is known.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the text that characterizes the application_context.

note.p: The description attribute aids in defining the usage of product data in an application_context.
This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to application_context as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994.

dd.p: the identifier that distinguishes the application_context.

note.p: This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to application_context as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994.

The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the set of instances of the entity data type application_context_element that defines the various aspects of the application_context.
Each application_context shall be the described_item in at most one description_attribute.

note.p: The description_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303.

dd.p: Each application_context shall be the identified_item in at most one id_attribute.

note.p: The id_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303.
A template for constraining the population of the entity data types defined in the basic_attribute_schema is described in annex E.

clause.title: application_context_element
clause.p: An application_context_element is an aspect of an application context that contains information about the context in which product data is defined. This aspect contains information about the conditions in which the product data exists.
An application_context_element may be either a library_context or a product_concept_context, or a product_context, or a product_definition_context.

dd.p: the label by which the application_context_element is known.

example.p: ‘Functional definition’, ‘physical definition’, ‘usage occurrence’, and ‘manufacturable definition’ are examples of names.

dd.p: the application_context of which this application_context_element is a member.

clause.title: application_context_relationship
clause.p:
An application_context_relationship is a relationship between two instances of application_context and provides a description of their relationship.
The role of application_context_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.
Without any further specialization, this relationship does not imply that the product data associated with relating_context are also associated with the related_context.
Relationships represented using this entity may be parent child relationship. Annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity specify whether or not the relationship is directed.
This entity, together with the application_context entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3.

dd.p: the label by which the application_context_relationship is known.
the text that characterizes the application_context_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
one of the instances of application_context that is a part of the relationship.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the other instance of application_context that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other, this attribute shall be the dependent one.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: application_protocol_definition
clause.p: An application_protocol_definition is the identification of an application protocol.

dd.p: the label that provides a user interpretable designation for the level of completion of the application protocol.

example.p: “IS”, “DIS”, “TS” or “CD” are examples of application protocol states.

dd.p: the EXPRESS schema name of the application interpreted model.
the year when the application protocol attained the status given by the status attribute.
the application context of the application protocol.

clause.title: library_context
clause.p: A library_context is a type of application_context_element that defines a context for elements of a library.

The inherited attribute name identifies or characterizes the type of library.
The name attribute can represent the nature of the source of the library, the nature of the contents of the library, or both.

example.p: ‘Dewey Decimal’, ‘ISO 13584 library’, and ‘supplier catalogue’ are examples of type of library.

dd.p: the label that identifies the library.

example.p: ‘ACME self-propelled rocket sleds catalogue’ is an example of a library reference.

clause.title: product_concept_context
clause.p: A product_concept_context is a type of application_context_element that defines a context for a product_concept (see ISO 10303-44).
A product_concept_context represents information that relates to the characterization of potential purchasers of a product. Such information may affect the meaning and usage of the product data.

dd.p: the label that identifies the kind of consumer preferences associated with a product.

example.p: ‘Luxury automobiles’, ‘laptop personal computers’, and ‘budget personal stereos’ are examples of *market_segment_type*s.

clause.title: product_context
clause.p:
A product_context is a type of application_context_element that represents life cycle independent information about a product. This information describes the discipline in which data about the product are created.
Different annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity data type can make use of common values for the attributes of the product_context entity data type in order to establish consistency among schemas that relate to the same types or kinds of products.

example.p: Two annotated EXPRESS schemas that specify product data structures for design and construction of buildings respectively can each constrain the values of the name attribute to be ‘building’, and the discipline_type attribute to be ‘architecture’.

clause.p:
The inherited attribute name identifies a particular industry, subject area, or kind of product for which product data is created or used.
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

example.p: ‘ship’, ‘aircraft’ and ‘building’ are examples of names of product contexts.

dd.p: the label that identifies a particular field of practice involved in creating or using product data.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

example.p: ‘electronics’, ‘engineering’, or ‘architecture’ are examples of discipline types.

clause.title: product_definition_context
clause.p:
A product_definition_context is a type of application_context_element that represents information about the stage in the product life cycle for which a product_definition is created or used.
Different annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity data type can make use of common values for the attributes of the product_definition_context entity data type in order to maintain consistency between schemas that relate to the same or related life-cycle phases.

example.p: Two annotated EXPRESS schemas that specify product data structures for conceptual design and detailed design of process plants respectively can each constrain the values of the name attribute to be ‘conceptual design’ and ‘detailed design’, and the life_cycle_stage attribute to be ‘design’.

clause.p:
The inherited attribute name identifies a subdivision or characterization of a life cycle stage for which product data is created or used.
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

example.p: ‘required’ and ‘planned’ are examples of names of product definition contexts, used in conjunction with a life cycle stage of ‘thermal analysis’.

dd.p: the label that identifies a stage in the life cycle of a product.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

example.p: A ‘preliminary design’ and ‘manufacturing planning’ are examples of life cycle stages.

clause.title: dependent_product_definition_exchange_context
clause.p: A dependent_product_definition_exchange_context is a type of product_definition_context and is an abstract entity that describes a specific context for exchange.

dd.p: at least one of the entities identification_dependent_product_definition_exchange_context or language_dependent_product_definition_exchange_context shall be specified.

clause.title: identification_dependent_product_definition_exchange_context
clause.p: An identification_dependent_product_definition_exchange_context is a type of dependent_product_definition_exchange_context that establishes the context of the product_definition exchange.

dd.p: specifies the context of the exchange to be either identification_assignment or organization .

clause.title: language_dependent_product_definition_exchange_context
clause.p: A language_dependent_product_definition_exchange_context is a type of dependent_product_definition_exchange_context that establishes the specified language of the product_definition exchange context.

dd.p: specifies the default language of the exchange context.

references.title: Normative references
references.p: There are no normative references in this document.
